tagline: From city streets to a canal-side dead end at Shell Beach.
intro: Louisiana Highway 46 runs east from New Orleans into St. Bernard Parish, following the Mississippi before turning toward Shell Beach. The highway carries the San Bernardo Scenic Byway name. Four divided lanes narrow to two at Paris Road in Chalmette; farther east, the road widens again before returning to two lanes for its final approach to Shell Beach.

San Bernardo was one of four communities founded by Canarians who arrived in Spanish Louisiana between 1778 and 1783. The community preserved much of its language and culture into the 21st century. The Spanish dialect brought from the Canary Islands is still spoken in St. Bernard Parish.

Begin on Elysian Fields Avenue, turn east onto St. Claude Avenue and cross the Industrial Canal. Arabi lies between the Lower 9th Ward and Chalmette on the Mississippi’s east bank. Beyond Chalmette, LA 46 shares two miles with LA 39, then turns east through Reggio. The journey ends at Shell Beach on the Mississippi River-Gulf Outlet Canal near Lake Borgne.

moments.title: Arabi
moments.text: Hotel dishes unearthed during swimming-pool excavations tell an unexpected part of Arabi’s stockyard history: table scraps from New Orleans hotels and restaurants once fed the animals here. The settlement began as Stockyard Landing, named for its stockyards and slaughterhouses. Those businesses also helped redraw the parish boundary. Seeking independence from New Orleans control, stockyard interests persuaded Louisiana to transfer the area downriver from Jackson Barracks to St. Bernard Parish in 1875. The mostly residential Friscoville Street Historic District includes a former casino, a historic jail, a church and a brick school.

moments.title: Chalmette Battlefield
moments.text: Chalmette preserves the site where Andrew Jackson’s forces defeated the British in January 1815. The American victory is only one part of this ground’s history. Fazendeville, an African American community with stores, a school and the Battle Ground Baptist Church, later occupied land here. In 1964, the parish government expropriated the land for park expansion. More than 50 families were forced to relocate when the National Park Service acquired it; demolition was completed in 1966. The visitor center near the battlefield obelisk is a replacement: it reopened in 2010 after Hurricane Katrina destroyed the earlier center.

moments.title: Shell Beach
moments.text: At Shell Beach, LA 46 reaches its eastern terminus beside the Mississippi River-Gulf Outlet Canal. The community lies near Lake Borgne, 18 miles east-southeast of Chalmette. Nearby Fort Proctor is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
